item.title: Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow
item.description:
Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow

The Milvus Vector Database project has released documentation and guidelines for its Python SDK, outlining installation methods, contribution processes, and version management practices.

📦 Installation & Requirements

PyMilvus supports Python 3.9+ and can be installed via pip or pip3. Specific versions of PyMilvus can be installed or upgraded to the latest release using pip commands.

🛠️ Development Workflow

Local development for the project uses the uv package manager, which must be installed before running make targets. The process includes:

  • Running pre-commit hooks to automatically execute linting and formatting checks before each commit.
  • Retrieving protos matching generated files, with specific version details available in milvus-proto.

🔄 Testing & Versioning

Commits on the development branch are packaged and uploaded to Test PyPI. The package naming convention for development branches follows the format x.y.z.rc<dist>, where <dist> represents the number of commits differing from the most recent release. Installing these packages requires appending --extra-index-url to the pip command.

💬 Community & Documentation

Contributors are encouraged to read contribution guidelines before adding code. For discussions or problem-solving, the community can be reached in the Slack channel #py-milvus. Documentation for PyMilvus is available online at the project’s API reference URL.

#Milvus #PythonSDK #VectorDatabase #DevOps #Programming

Source: milvus-io/pymilvus

item.title: Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released
item.description:
Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released

The official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients has been released, providing a Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The documentation is available at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/, including a Get started guide, What’s new in v2, the API reference, and a migration guide.

🔍 Overview

  • The Model Context Protocol lets you build servers that expose data and functionality to LLM applications in a secure, standardized way.
  • Think of it like a web API, but designed for LLM interactions.

🧩 How it works

  • Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts to any MCP host.
  • Build MCP clients that connect to any MCP server.
  • Speak every standard transport: stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE.
  • Python 3.11+ is required.

⚙️ Key details

  • The cli extra adds the mcp command-line tool (mcp dev, mcp run, mcp install) on top of the SDK; install plain mcp if you don’t need it.
  • For one-off commands, uv run --with "mcp[cli]" mcp ... works without a project.
  • Example usage: Add two numbers or greet someone by name.
  • That’s a complete MCP server: one tool, one templated resource.
  • Call add with a=1, b=2 and you get 3 back.
  • Notice what you did not write: no JSON Schema (a: int, b: int is the schema), no request parsing, no validation code, no protocol handling.
  • Two type-hinted Python functions and a docstring.
  • The same package is a full MCP client.
  • A URL means Streamable HTTP, the transport you deploy.
  • Client can also launch a local server as a stdio subprocess or take any custom transport.

🚀 Availability

  • The project is licensed under the MIT License.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing guide to get started.

💡 Why it matters

  • The SDK simplifies building and connecting to MCP servers and clients, reducing the need for manual request parsing, validation, and protocol handling.
  • It supports various transports, making it versatile for different deployment scenarios.
  • The project aims to support contributors of all levels of experience.

#PythonSDK #ModelContextProtocol #LLMApplications #AITools

Source: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

item.title: LiteLLM Open Source AI Gateway Launches for 100+ LLM Providers
item.description:
LiteLLM Open Source AI Gateway Launches for 100+ LLM Providers

LiteLLM, an open source AI Gateway, has been released, offering a unified interface to call over 100 LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, and more, using the OpenAI format.

🔍 Overview

LiteLLM provides a single, centralized interface to interact with multiple LLM providers, eliminating the need for provider-specific SDKs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Unified API for 100+ LLMs, enabling seamless switching between providers without code changes
  • Drop-in OpenAI compatibility
  • Production-ready gateway with features such as:
    • Virtual keys
    • Spend tracking
    • Guardrails
    • Load balancing
    • Admin dashboard
  • Performance: 8ms P95 latency at 1k requests per second
  • Supports all OpenAI endpoints: /chat/completions, /responses, /embeddings, /images, /audio, /batches, /rerank, /a2a, /messages
  • Rust core with Python SDK

🚀 Availability

  • Deployable as a Python SDK for direct library integration
  • Deployable as an AI Gateway (Proxy Server) for teams or organizations
  • Installation via uv add litellm

#LiteLLM #AIgateway #LLM #OpenAI #PythonSDK #ProxyServer
